messages.body_plain:
Dear Tony,

Could you clarify what you mean by 'selected the transitions based on replicates'? Could you confirm that you have multiple distinct MS runs per condition?

There is indeed not much change in group comparison, however there is a change in how transitions are summarized within a MS run. I suspect that you may have some borderline situation in your experiment. For example, if you do not have distinct MS runs, MSstats 2.6 reported the p-value but it was too optimistic (In this case the dataset does not have the information on the between-run variation, and the p-value in MSstats 2.6 assumed that the within-run variation is the only source of uncertainty.) This was meant to be used as an indication only, but we now understand that many researchers were unaware of the fact that the between-run variation is most important. Therefore, to prevent false optimism, MSstats 3 retired this option. Now we only output p-values in presence of replicate MS runs for each condition.

Does this address your question?
Sincerely
Olga

messages.body_plain:
Dear Tony,

Both normalization and missing value handling are performed at run level.

(1) Normalization using the 'globalStandards' option is based on the log intensities of the selected standard peptides and/or proteins (provided in the 'nameStandards' option). Briefly, it takes three steps: (a) get the mean of features for each standard (in each run), (b) get the mean among all standards (in each run), (c) equalizing the mean calculated in step (b) to the median across runs.

(2) Missing values are also handled at run level. Some more details are described in an earlier thread:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!starred/msstats/ajaMGYJgNZI

Hope this helps
Tsung-Heng
